title: Install / update / remove / rollback receipt
description: One receipt per lifecycle action (spec 10858). The receipt is the ROLLBACK SOURCE: `previous` records what was installed before, so rollback is a replay of recorded state rather than a re-resolution against a registry that may have changed underneath. It also records every GATE that was evaluated with its outcome -- an install that refuses must say which of the eleven gates refused, because a single opaque `failed` is what turns a security control into folklore.

outcome.description: Terminal states only (AGENTS.md section 4). REFUSED is a policy decision and is the CORRECT outcome for a revoked or over-permissioned package; FAILED is an error. Collapsing them would make a working security control look like a bug.

overrides_used.description: An override that is not recorded is an override nobody can audit.

refusal_code.description: Stable machine code for the refusing gate, so a caller can branch on WHY without parsing prose.
